network.overall_strategy: Construct an evidence-graded network containing ten distinct reaction sequences, not ten independently demonstrated prebiotic syntheses. P1 follows the reported cyanosulfidic construction of the proline aminonitrile, followed by chemically expected but unquantified hydrolysis. P2-P8 are explicitly speculative mechanistic alternatives involving nitrile reduction, sulfurization, cyclization, or sulfur-assisted hydrolysis. P9-P10 explore a glutamate/P5C route and contain an explicitly unresolved carboxylate-reduction step; they are research hypotheses, not established syntheses. Small C2/C3 keto acids are supplied feedstocks for those two paths, not claimed products of CO2 fixation. All achiral routes produce L-proline together with D-proline; separate stereoisomer nodes prevent a racemate from being mislabeled as enantiopure L-proline. This network therefore reaches L-proline as a racemate component, not isolated or selectively synthesized L-proline. No demonstrated prebiotic resolution step is supplied: proline phase amplification requires an initial bias, and the strongest reported enrichment used non-prebiotic chloroform (Klussmann et al., 2006). Conditions are proposed geological operating windows unless explicitly identified as experimental observations; detailed Patel et al. procedures were not independently verified from their supplementary information. Neutral formulas represent acid-base reference species. S8 is an idealized endpoint for oxidized sulfur, not a claim that every photoreaction exclusively produces molecular S8. Null formation environments indicate supplied feedstocks or species formed in multiple environments. No oxygen, enzymes, or unsupported mineral catalysts are assumed. Detection-only discharge and extraterrestrial results are not converted into invented intermediate-resolved reactions.

reactions.name: Copper(I)-catalyzed acetylene hydrocyanation

conditions.other: Anoxic gas-liquid contact; conduct before sulfide-rich processing to limit copper sulfide precipitation. Exact experimental catalyst loading is not supplied.

reactions.mechanism: Copper-mediated addition of HCN across acetylene produces the C3 unsaturated nitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Supported in the supplied account of Patel et al. (2015). Cu(I) has a reaction-specific role rather than being an arbitrary mineral additive. Acetylene availability, local copper concentration, cyanide speciation, and staged delivery remain geochemical constraints. Acetylene is supplied here; its proposed carbide source is not assumed to have been demonstrated.

reactions.name: Ammonia aza-Michael addition to acrylonitrile

conditions.other: Ammonia-rich solution; proposed pH 8-10. Limit prolonged exposure that could favor oligomerization or repeated alkylation.

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia adds conjugatively to the activated alkene, followed by proton transfer.
reactions.reasoning: This branch is described by Patel et al. (2015). It introduces the nitrogen ultimately retained in the pyrrolidine ring. Cyanamide is not included because guanidinylation would divert this branch toward arginine-related precursors rather than improve proline formation.

reactions.name: Photoreductive conversion of beta-aminopropionitrile to its aldehyde

conditions.other: UV irradiation; 254 nm is the laboratory analogue. H2S/HS- supplies reducing equivalents. Proposed near-neutral to mildly alkaline conditions; no molecular oxygen.

reactions.mechanism: Photochemical nitrile reduction gives an imine that hydrolyzes to the aldehyde, releasing ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Supported in outline by Patel et al. (2015); exact proline-branch conditions require supplementary-information verification. Copper acceleration is not assumed because sulfide-driven chemistry can operate without it. Sulfur is represented by an idealized S8 endpoint; actual sulfur speciation and photon efficiency require measurement. Sulfide availability is constrained by Ranjan et al. (2018).

reactions.name: Cyanohydrin homologation of beta-aminopropionaldehyde

conditions.other: HCN/CN- availability with controlled addition; proposed pH 7-9. Minimize aldehyde residence time before capture.

reactions.mechanism: Cyanide attacks the aldehyde and protonation produces a racemic cyanohydrin.
reactions.reasoning: This C1 homologation is part of the sequence summarized from Patel et al. (2015). It gives the four-carbon precursor needed for a five-membered nitrogen heterocycle. An achiral environment provides no basis for assigning one cyanohydrin configuration preferentially.

reactions.name: Cyanohydrin sulfurization and cyclic hydroxythioamide formation

conditions.other: Sulfide-bearing solution; staged equilibration. Exact pH and cyclic-to-open-chain product ratio are not specified in the supplied evidence.

reactions.mechanism: Sulfide addition to the nitrile generates an open-chain hydroxythioamide; intramolecular aminolysis forms the five-membered thiolactam and releases ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015), as summarized, observed cyclic and open-chain alpha-hydroxythioamides. This is a net reaction node combining sulfur addition and ring closure, not a claim that the cyclic product forms exclusively or in one elementary step. The unproven productive fate of the open-chain coproduct is not separately counted as a pathway.

reactions.name: Photodeoxygenation of the cyclic hydroxythioamide

conditions.other: UV irradiation with continuing H2S/HS- supply; 254 nm laboratory analogue. Irradiation dose under realistic solar spectra is unresolved.

reactions.mechanism: Photoreductive replacement of the alpha-hydroxyl group by hydrogen gives gamma-butyrothiolactam.
reactions.reasoning: The supplied Patel et al. (2015) account identifies the cyclic thiolactam as the only deoxygenated thioamide detected in this mixture. Sulfide is a reducing reagent, not an unspecified mineral catalyst. Geochemical sulfide availability and realistic irradiation rates remain bottlenecks (Ranjan et al., 2018).

reactions.name: Thiolactam photoreduction through an inferred cyclic imine

conditions.other: UV/H2S photoreductive medium; rapid subsequent HCN capture. H2S occurs on both sides because reductant oxidation and release of substrate sulfur as H2S can cancel in the formal net balance.

reactions.mechanism: Reduction and sulfur elimination are represented as passing through 1-pyrroline before cyanide capture.
reactions.reasoning: The thiolactam-to-aminonitrile conversion is supported by Patel et al. (2015), but the supplied review explicitly identifies free 1-pyrroline as inferred rather than isolated. Separating this node from HCN capture is mechanistic bookkeeping. Neither an isolated imine yield nor an exclusive S8 coproduct distribution is established.

reactions.name: Cyclic Strecker capture of 1-pyrroline

conditions.other: HCN addition during or immediately after imine generation; competing imine hydrolysis must be limited.

reactions.mechanism: Cyanide attacks the cyclic imine or iminium carbon, creating the proline aminonitrile stereocenter without enantioselection.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) reported the proline aminonitrile; the supplied account gives 32% over two late precursor-forming steps, not a yield for isolated 1-pyrroline or proline. Ritson (2021) notes unusual resistance of this cyclic aminonitrile to retro-Strecker conversion under conditions that destabilize acyclic analogues. Its formation is racemic.

reactions.name: Acid-catalyzed proline aminonitrile hydration

conditions.other: Acidic geothermal pool, proposed pH 1-3; transition to hydrolysis only after aminonitrile formation. Required duration and conversion are unknown.

reactions.mechanism: Nitrile protonation, water addition, and tautomerization produce the carboxamide.
reactions.reasoning: Chemically expected but unquantified for this network. The supplied Patel et al. (2015) account stops at the aminonitrile and does not establish a prolinamide yield. Ritson (2021) supports precursor retention, not a measured hydration rate. The proposed conditions are a testable hypothesis rather than a reproduced prebiotic protocol.

reactions.name: Prolinamide hydrolysis to racemic proline

conditions.other: Sustained acidic aqueous residence; acid-base forms of ammonia and proline are implicit. No stereochemical separation is assumed.

reactions.mechanism: Water attacks the activated amide carbonyl, and ammonia departure gives the carboxylic acid.
reactions.reasoning: Standard amide-hydrolysis chemistry supplies a plausible final conversion, but the provided research contains no end-to-end hydrolysis yield from the Patel et al. (2015) proline precursor. This is an unquantified bottleneck. L- and D-proline are both outputs because racemic precursor hydrolysis does not establish homochirality.

reactions.name: Candidate conjugate hydrocyanation of acrylonitrile

conditions.other: Proposed pH 8-10 supplies a nucleophilic cyanide fraction. Competing acrylonitrile polymerization and reversibility require measurement.

reactions.mechanism: Conjugate cyanide addition followed by protonation generates the C4 dinitrile skeleton.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative as a prebiotic network edge: no supplied study demonstrates this reaction under the stated geological conditions. It is included because an activated alkene and cyanide provide a chemically direct alternative to the aldehyde/cyanohydrin homologation, not because Patel et al. (2015) established this branch.

reactions.name: Candidate selective monoreduction of succinonitrile
agents: Native nickel or a nickel-rich metallic surface

conditions.pressure: 10-100 bar total pressure with an H2-rich fluid
conditions.other: Sulfide-poor rock-water pocket; short residence and limited conversion would be needed to suppress reduction of both nitriles.

reactions.mechanism: Surface hydrogenation converts one nitrile into a primary amine while retaining the other nitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative and selectivity-limited. Nickel can activate H2, but the supplied literature does not demonstrate prebiotic succinonitrile monoreduction. Kaur et al. (2024) support nickel/H2 amino-acid-related chemistry, not this substrate or selectivity. Diamine formation, cyclization, overreduction, and nickel poisoning could prevent useful accumulation.

reactions.name: Candidate photoreductive hydrolysis of gamma-aminobutyronitrile

conditions.other: UV/H2S exposure after transfer from a sulfide-poor reduction setting; 254 nm laboratory analogue. Minimize aldehyde residence time.

reactions.mechanism: Partial nitrile reduction followed by imine hydrolysis gives 4-aminobutanal.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative substrate extension of the nitrile photoreduction chemistry described by Patel et al. (2015). No supplied experiment establishes this gamma-amino substrate conversion. Sulfur addition and five-membered thiolactam formation may outcompete aldehyde production; rxn_015-rxn_016 explicitly represent that chemically different possibility.

reactions.name: 4-Aminobutanal cyclocondensation

conditions.other: Near-neutral solution with immediate HCN trapping; dilution and imine hydrolysis compete with net accumulation.

reactions.mechanism: The terminal amino group attacks the aldehyde, followed by dehydration to the five-membered cyclic imine.
reactions.reasoning: Chemically well-motivated intramolecular imine formation, but not an isolated discharge intermediate established by the supplied sources. Ring et al. (1972) support proline detection, not this mechanistic assignment. Its role here is conditional on independently producing 4-aminobutanal.

reactions.name: Candidate sulfurization of gamma-aminobutyronitrile

conditions.other: Sulfide-bearing concentrated solution; proposed mildly alkaline conditions. No ultraviolet requirement is assumed for the addition step.

reactions.mechanism: Hydrosulfide addition to the nitrile and proton transfer form the open-chain thioamide.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative for this substrate. Patel et al. (2015) provide related nitrile-to-thioamide chemistry, but do not establish this branch in the supplied account. It is chemically motivated by the same sulfur nucleophile and provides a testable alternative to attempting selective aldehyde production.

reactions.name: Candidate cyclization of gamma-aminobutanethioamide

conditions.other: Concentrating geothermal pool; proposed moderate pH allowing a nucleophilic terminal amine. Ammonia removal could favor ring closure.

reactions.mechanism: Intramolecular attack on the thiocarbonyl followed by ammonia elimination produces a five-membered thiolactam.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative but supported by favorable ring geometry and the related hydroxythioamide cyclization reported by Patel et al. (2015). The unsubstituted open-chain thioamide is not demonstrated as a productive precursor in the supplied research. Rate, equilibrium position, and competing hydrolysis remain unknown.

reactions.name: Candidate partial hydrogenation and intramolecular transimination
agents: Native nickel or a nickel-rich metallic surface

conditions.pressure: 10-100 bar total pressure with controlled H2 activity
conditions.other: Sulfide-poor pocket; imine must desorb and leave the reducing zone before further hydrogenation. HCN capture is assigned to a subsequent surface stage.

reactions.mechanism: Partial nitrile hydrogenation gives an open-chain imine; intramolecular transimination releases ammonia and forms 1-pyrroline.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative: no supplied study demonstrates this route under prebiotic conditions. The mechanism avoids an aldehyde intermediate, making it distinct from rxn_013-rxn_014. Nickel/H2 plausibility alone is insufficient evidence (Kaur et al., 2024); overreduction to pyrrolidine or formation of a diamine may dominate.

reactions.name: Candidate sulfur-assisted conversion of proline aminonitrile to thioamide

conditions.other: Concentrated sulfide-bearing solution; proposed pH 8-10. Assess aminonitrile recovery and competing reactions explicitly.

reactions.mechanism: Sulfide adds to the exocyclic nitrile, giving the corresponding carbothioamide without changing the pyrrolidine skeleton.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative alternative to direct nitrile hydration. Patel et al. (2015) support related thioamide chemistry, not this proline substrate transformation. Ritson (2021) supports unusual aminonitrile persistence but does not establish sulfur-assisted hydrolysis. No rate advantage or yield improvement is asserted.

reactions.name: Candidate prolinethioamide hydrolysis

conditions.other: Acidic geothermal water after sulfurization; prolonged residence may be required. Net hydrolysis consumes two waters per thioamide.

reactions.mechanism: Hydrolytic replacement of sulfur and subsequent amide cleavage yield the carboxylic acid, hydrogen sulfide, and ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative for prebiotic prolinethioamide: no supplied study demonstrates this conversion or its rate. The net chemistry is a chemically reasonable sulfur-assisted alternative, not an established extension of Patel et al. (2015). A prolinamide intermediate may occur transiently; the node represents the overall hydrolysis sequence. Both proline enantiomers remain present.

reactions.name: Candidate aldol assembly of a C5 hydroxy keto acid
agents: Hydroxide ions as a proposed general-base catalyst

conditions.other: Concentrated pyruvate and glyoxylate; proposed pH 8-10. Competing self-condensation, hydration, and decomposition require measurement.

reactions.mechanism: A pyruvate-derived enol or enolate attacks glyoxylate, producing 4-hydroxy-2-oxoglutarate.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative stepwise assignment in this network. Kaur et al. (2024) support coupling reductive aldol keto-acid generation with amino-acid chemistry, but the supplied summary does not verify isolation of this intermediate under these conditions. This edge provides a chemically motivated C2+C3 supply hypothesis rather than assuming an unexplained C5 feedstock.

reactions.name: Candidate selective reductive deoxygenation to alpha-ketoglutarate
agents: Native nickel or a nickel-rich metallic surface

conditions.other: Sulfide-poor conditions. Desired hydroxyl removal must compete successfully with reduction of the keto group and carbon-carbon bond cleavage.

reactions.mechanism: Net replacement of the C4 hydroxyl group by hydrogen generates alpha-ketoglutarate.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative substrate-specific edge. The reductive aldol framework discussed by Kaur et al. (2024) motivates testing this connection but does not, in the supplied summary, establish this isolated transformation. Selective deoxygenation while retaining an alpha-keto acid is a substantial unresolved requirement.

reactions.name: Metal-catalyzed reductive amination of alpha-ketoglutarate

conditions.temperature: 350-373 K proposed; the cited mild nickel study operated near 295 K
conditions.pressure: 10-100 bar total pressure; proposed H2 partial pressure 1-5 bar
conditions.other: Proposed pH 8-10 and locally concentrated ammonium/ammonia. Maintain a reduced, sulfide-poor catalytic surface.

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia condensation with the alpha-keto group followed by hydrogenation gives glutamate.
reactions.reasoning: Glutamate formation by abiotic reductive amination has experimental support from Kitadai et al. (2019) and Kaur et al. (2024). The stated warmer hydrothermal window is an extrapolation, not a reproduced yield claim. These studies support glutamate formation only; they do not establish the subsequent proline steps. Achiral catalysis gives racemic glutamate.

reactions.name: Unresolved glutamate side-chain carboxylate reduction

conditions.temperature: Not established; 350-400 K is only a possible screening window
conditions.pressure: Not established; an H2-rich pressurized aqueous setting is hypothetical
conditions.other: No validated nonenzymatic activating agent or selective reducing system is supplied. This edge explicitly denotes an unresolved research gap, not an executable reaction.

reactions.mechanism: Formal reduction of the side-chain carboxyl group to an aldehyde while retaining the alpha-carboxyl group.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative and currently unsupported as a prebiotic synthesis. Biological glutamate reduction requires activation and reducing cofactors (Fichman et al., 2015). The supplied review identifies no mineral or metal system accomplishing this selective conversion. Favorable overall amino-acid formation energetics cannot remove this kinetic and activation barrier (Amend and Shock, 1998). Consequently P9 and P10 are not established complete chemical routes.

reactions.name: Spontaneous glutamate semialdehyde cyclization

conditions.temperature: 350-373 K proposed for a cool hydrothermal compartment
conditions.other: Near-neutral to mildly alkaline aqueous conditions; short residence before further reaction. The cited spontaneous cyclization is not specific to this pressure-temperature window.

reactions.mechanism: Intramolecular amino-aldehyde condensation closes a five-membered ring and eliminates water.
reactions.reasoning: Spontaneous, strongly favored GSA/P5C interconversion is supported by Smith and Greenberg (1956). No enzyme is needed for this ring closure. This established local transformation does not solve GSA supply, and its inclusion must not be interpreted as evidence for the preceding carboxylate reduction.

reactions.name: Candidate nickel-hydrogen reduction of P5C

conditions.other: Sulfide-poor conditions; monitor substrate adsorption, decomposition, and recovery. No biological reductase or modern hydride reagent is used.

reactions.mechanism: Hydrogenation of the cyclic imine bond yields the saturated pyrrolidine ring.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative prebiotic implementation. P5C reduction is chemically plausible, but the supplied review found no demonstrated H2/Ni prebiotic conversion to proline. Kaur et al. (2024) justify investigating nickel/H2 chemistry, not assigning a P5C yield. Racemic GSA/P5C supply gives both proline enantiomers; reduction does not create an L-selective route.

reactions.name: Candidate sulfide photoreduction of P5C

conditions.other: Requires delivery of P5C-containing fluid into a UV-accessible sulfide-bearing pool. Use a 254 nm laboratory analogue only as a test system; realistic solar performance is unknown.

reactions.mechanism: Proposed photogenerated reducing equivalents hydrogenate the cyclic imine while sulfide is oxidized.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative: Patel et al. (2015) demonstrate related sulfide photoreduction chemistry, but the supplied review found no prebiotic P5C-to-proline demonstration. This is mechanistically distinct from nickel/H2 hydrogenation. P5C photodegradation, sulfide addition, and geochemical sulfide limitations could defeat the proposed reduction (Ranjan et al., 2018). No enantioselection is predicted.

pathways.name: Reported cyanosulfidic skeleton construction with conventional hydrolysis
pathways.description: Best-supported intermediate-resolved skeleton route. The cyclic imine is inferred, and aminonitrile-to-proline hydrolysis remains unquantified. Produces L-proline within a racemate, not selectively.

pathways.name: Cyanosulfidic skeleton construction with candidate sulfur-assisted hydrolysis
pathways.description: Shares P1's skeleton chemistry but replaces conventional nitrile hydration with an unvalidated prolinethioamide route. A distinct mechanistic variant, not an independently demonstrated synthesis.

pathways.name: Candidate succinonitrile-to-aminoaldehyde route with conventional hydrolysis
pathways.description: Builds the C4 skeleton by conjugate hydrocyanation, selectively reduces one nitrile, and photoreductively converts the remaining nitrile to an aminoaldehyde before cyclic Strecker capture. Several substrate-specific steps are unvalidated.

pathways.name: Candidate succinonitrile-to-aminoaldehyde route with sulfur-assisted hydrolysis
pathways.description: Uses P3's speculative aminoaldehyde entry and a second unvalidated branch through prolinethioamide. No end-to-end experimental support or L-selectivity is claimed.

pathways.name: Candidate succinonitrile-to-thiolactam route with conventional hydrolysis
pathways.description: Avoids selective aminoaldehyde production by sulfurizing gamma-aminobutyronitrile and attempting thiolactam formation. Converges on the reported thiolactam chemistry, but the alternative entry is unvalidated.

pathways.name: Candidate succinonitrile-to-thiolactam route with sulfur-assisted hydrolysis
pathways.description: Combines the unvalidated thiolactam entry with unvalidated sulfur-assisted aminonitrile hydrolysis. Distinct by reaction sequence, but shares most chemistry with P5.

pathways.name: Candidate hydrogenative transimination route with conventional hydrolysis
pathways.description: Attempts to obtain 1-pyrroline directly from gamma-aminobutyronitrile by partial hydrogenation and intramolecular transimination. Avoids aldehyde and thiolactam intermediates but faces severe overreduction and trapping challenges.

pathways.name: Candidate hydrogenative transimination route with sulfur-assisted hydrolysis
pathways.description: Combines direct hydrogenative cyclic-imine formation with the prolinethioamide finishing hypothesis. Both distinctive branches lack demonstration in the supplied research.

pathways.name: Conditional keto-acid/glutamate route with nickel-hydrogen P5C reduction
pathways.description: Starts from supplied C2/C3 keto acids. Glutamate reductive amination and GSA cyclization have support, but C5 precursor assembly is provisional, glutamate-to-GSA reduction is explicitly unresolved, and P5C hydrogenation is unvalidated. This is a research trajectory rather than an established complete synthesis.

pathways.name: Conditional keto-acid/glutamate route with sulfide photoreduction of P5C
pathways.description: Shares P9's unresolved precursor chemistry but substitutes a genuinely different photoreductive finishing hypothesis. Requires transfer to a UV-accessible environment and does not solve either glutamate activation or proline homochirality.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the strongest pathway. Its aminonitrile construction follows the supplied account of Patel et al. (2015), including the reported 32% yield over the final two precursor-forming steps. The discrete 1-pyrroline intermediate remains inferred. Aminonitrile hydration and amide hydrolysis are conventional chemistry, but their rates, yields and compatibility with the preceding mixture are not established here. Surface labels alone do not specify the necessary operating conditions. L-proline is plausibly obtained as a racemate component; the absence of resolution is not treated as failure of that explicitly stated objective.
suggestions: Attach reaction-specific Patel et al. citations and verified procedures, distinguishing observed products from inferred intermediates.
Demonstrate rxn_009 and rxn_010 with specified pH, temperature and residence time, measuring free proline separately from hydrolyzable precursors.

Specify reagent staging and copper speciation in sulfide-containing media. In rxn_007, H2S cancels from the balanced equation; clarify its photochemical role without interpreting that bookkeeping as proof of a catalytic mechanism.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P2 retains the evidence-supported aminonitrile construction but adds an unvalidated sulfur-assisted finishing sequence. Nitrile sulfurization and thioamide hydrolysis are chemically recognizable transformations, and both equations conserve mass. However, the network does not establish that this substrate sulfurizes efficiently or that its thioamide hydrolyzes faster or under more suitable conditions than the original nitrile. Acknowledging these uncertainties is appropriate but does not establish productive flux to proline.
suggestions: Measure prolinethioamide formation and hydrolysis under explicit sulfide concentration, pH and temperature conditions.
Track prolinamide alongside prolinethioamide and free proline to determine whether sulfurization actually improves the finishing sequence.
Retain the conventional hydrolysis route as the better-supported comparator rather than assuming sulfur-assisted hydrolysis is advantageous.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Conjugate cyanide addition to acrylonitrile is plausible, and 4-aminobutanal cyclization followed by Strecker capture is coherent. The principal enabling uncertainty is rxn_012: a catalyst and operating window that provide useful gamma-aminobutyronitrile flux rather than extensive further reduction are not specified. Reaction rxn_013 extrapolates established photoreductive chemistry to a different substrate. Transfers of succinonitrile into the hydrothermal setting and amino nitrile back to the surface lack transport and survival justification.
suggestions: Specify cyanide speciation and quantify succinonitrile formation against competing acrylonitrile reactions.
Identify an available hydrogenation catalyst and measure amino-nitrile, diamine and cyclic-product yields as functions of hydrogen activity and residence time.
Demonstrate rxn_013 and physically justify intermediate transport, including dilution and survival.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The carbon-skeleton sequence is coherent, but it combines the unestablished selective hydrogenation and substrate-specific photoreduction of P3 with the unvalidated sulfur-assisted finishing sequence of P2. None of these reactions violates the supplied conservation check. Nevertheless, their serial combination does not establish a working synthesis, and the proposed environment labels do not establish catalyst availability, transport or compatible sulfurization and hydrolysis conditions.
suggestions: Validate the succinonitrile-to-pyrroline sequence before relying on the additional sulfur-assisted finishing reactions.
Compare conventional and sulfur-assisted hydrolysis using the same aminonitrile-containing mixture.
Provide transfer conditions and a reagent-staging schedule supported by intermediate stability measurements.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This pathway could connect an amino nitrile to the literature-supported thiolactam branch, but its entrance reactions remain conditional. Sulfurization is plausible, whereas rxn_016 requires demonstrated intramolecular thioamide substitution with ammonia elimination; favorable five-membered ring formation alone does not establish that transformation. Selective succinonitrile reduction remains an upstream bottleneck. The conventional hydrolysis endpoint is credible but unquantified.
suggestions: Specify mol_022 structurally as H2N(CH2)3C(=S)NH2 and directly verify thiolactam formation and ammonia release in rxn_016.
Determine whether the cyclization conditions preserve the amino thioamide and suppress competing products.
Establish useful amino-nitrile production and survival during transfer from hydrogenation to surface sulfur chemistry.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P6 is a coherent research hypothesis but depends on several unverified enabling transformations: selective dinitrile reduction, amino-thioamide cyclization and sulfur-assisted aminonitrile hydrolysis. Reaching gamma-butyrothiolactam would connect to an experimentally supported precursor-forming segment, but that support does not validate the proposed upstream or downstream reactions. Sulfide participation in multiple steps does not by itself establish compatible operating conditions.
suggestions: Validate rxn_012 and rxn_016 as separate enabling reactions before testing the integrated sequence.
Measure sulfur speciation and product distributions rather than treating S8 bookkeeping as a mechanistic description.
Demonstrate that the actual thiolactam-derived aminonitrile mixture undergoes rxn_018 and rxn_019 productively.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Partial nitrile hydrogenation followed by intramolecular transimination is mechanistically plausible and atom-balanced. The difficulty is accumulating pyrroline under conditions capable of reducing nitriles: the cyclic imine may undergo further hydrogenation to pyrrolidine before HCN capture. This selectivity problem compounds the preceding selective monoreduction requirement. No catalyst, hydrogen activity, quenching procedure or pyrroline transport lifetime is supplied.
suggestions: Measure pyrroline accumulation against diamine and pyrrolidine formation under specified hydrogenation conditions.
Demonstrate catalyst separation or reaction termination followed by timely HCN capture, rather than assuming the imine survives transfer.
Establish that useful selectivity is possible at both hydrogenation stages without introducing an unspecified catalyst.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P8 inherits the unresolved hydrogenation selectivity and pyrroline-survival problems of P7, then adds an unvalidated sulfur-assisted finishing sequence. The molecular connections and conservation bookkeeping are valid, but no evidence establishes that sufficient flux can pass through these successive selectivity gates. The speculative designation is accurate and improves literature honesty, not chemical validation.
suggestions: First establish pyrroline generation and HCN trapping with a measured material balance.
Test sulfur-assisted hydrolysis independently against conventional hydrolysis before integrating it.
Specify catalyst handling, hydrogen removal, sulfide introduction and transfer conditions without assuming the different reaction mixtures are mutually compatible.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The supplied keto-acid feedstocks are acceptable, and the C5 skeleton is coherent. Keto-acid reductive amination has experimental support, while glutamate semialdehyde cyclization is well established. However, rxn_023 is an unresolved enabling gap: selective aqueous glutamate side-chain carboxylate reduction cannot be assumed from H2 availability. Nickel-mediated P5C reduction is chemically plausible but not demonstrated under prebiotic conditions in the supplied review. Downstream plausibility cannot overcome the missing semialdehyde-forming step.
suggestions: Keep the pathway explicitly conditional until rxn_023 is demonstrated, or specify and validate an activation sequence including its reagents and balanced byproducts.
Investigate whether rxn_021 proceeds through dehydration followed by alkene hydrogenation; specify the catalyst and selectivity relative to keto-group reduction.
Test P5C hydrogenation separately and attach substrate-specific evidence to rxn_022, distinguishing the Kitadai et al. and Kaur et al. operating conditions.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P10 remains blocked by rxn_023 and additionally requires substrate-specific validation of sulfide photoreduction and survival during P5C transfer to the surface. Reaction rxn_026 is chemically conceivable and balanceable, but the supplied literature does not demonstrate it. The checker's 7:1 L:D coefficient solution is only an elemental-balancing artifact; it provides no evidence for enantioenrichment and does not match the network's stated racemic outcome.
suggestions: Resolve glutamate-to-semialdehyde formation before presenting this branch as an operative route to proline.
Measure P5C photoreduction yield, competing losses and survival during transport under specified UV spectrum, sulfide concentration and pH.
Encode racemic stoichiometry explicitly for rxn_026: 8 mol_030 + 8 mol_005 -> 4 mol_016 + 4 mol_017 + mol_006. This remains consistent with the conservation check.

evaluation.network_feedback: The network is structurally strong: network validity is approximately 0.97, with sufficient nodes, consistent molecule references and a connected graph. Accepting the deterministic check as ground truth, all 26 reactions conserve atoms and charge with appropriate coefficients; there are no conservation violations. Multiples of eight arising from the S8 reference endpoint are not intrinsically implausible. Explicit coefficients should nevertheless be recorded, with stereochemical product ratios constrained independently of elemental balancing. Literature alignment is good, approximately 0.83: the network appropriately distinguishes reported precursor chemistry, inferred intermediates, speculative alternatives, unquantified hydrolysis and unresolved carboxylate reduction. It also correctly avoids converting detection-only studies into invented mechanisms. However, reaction-specific citations and verified experimental procedures are largely absent. The strongest chemical support concerns the P1 aminonitrile-forming sequence, not a demonstrated end-to-end geological synthesis of free proline. Conventional hydrolysis makes L-proline production as a racemate component credible, but its performance in the actual reaction mixture remains unmeasured. P2-P8 require additional selectivity and substrate-specific evidence; P9-P10 are blocked by rxn_023. Environmental assessment is limited because the submitted records provide broad environment labels rather than numerical conditions, catalyst availability, reagent staging or physically justified transfers. Copper speciation in sulfidic media, hydrogenation catalyst activity, hydrolysis conditions and intermediate survival require explicit treatment. These scores assess the complete network through its supported route and enabling bottlenecks, not by averaging duplicated pathway variants or rewarding any feedstock, framework, hub count or environmental order. This is a useful evidence-graded research network, but overall confidence is below the 0.90 network approval threshold.
